headToHead.voiceVerdict: Tie on the twelve. The downward pivot is now a real sentence shape: cover the names on Sorry/Agreed, nod, private jet, the joke/hi opener and the router line and nobody else in the cast says them, because the shape (claim, flinch, smaller claim, cheerful lock-in) is Dash's and not just the jargon. Liam's formal-clause-on-trivia register is equally unmistakable in every line he has. Two of our twelve still lean on vocabulary rather than shape (the Quill roast and 'open to acquisition' would survive as any rival's roast with the words swapped), which is why it is a tie and not a win.
headToHead.constructionVerdict: Ours. Punch on the last word nearly every time (concert, fifth, nod, router, market, March, font), real turns, nothing in the twelve explains itself. Liam's set is looser: the time-machine line has no turn, one is a paraphrase, and three are narrator lines doing his work for him.
headToHead.quotableVerdict: Bar. 'Save me from the consequences of my actions!' and the 360-degree spin are lines the fandom actually repeats, because Liam is wrong about himself in a way anyone recognises without knowing what a hipster is. Ours has two of that kind ('I request it twice, so it's a concert', 'together on the fifth'), where Dash's logic is airtight to him and wrong to everyone else. The rest of our clip-worthy lines ('buying the dip', 'click rate is lawsuits', 'open to acquisition') are jargon puns that need startup literacy to land and are funny about the vocabulary, not about the man.

templates: Jargon swap: a romance beat renamed as a startup term and left there as the joke (about 20 lines): ship/patch/roll back, private beta/monopoly, IPO, going public/user base/churn, buying the dip, shorting sorry, open rate, pipeline, ground-floor opportunity, child process to market, product-market fit, case study, soft launch forever, hockey stick. The vocabulary is Dash's; the comic engine is a pun any writer applies to any bot by swapping the glossary (Tilly's tickets, Nav's routes).

Countdown list: '[unit N], X. [unit N+1], Y. [unit N+2], Z.' (6 lines): 'launches Friday. Early access Thursday... Wednesday', 'Smile ships by nine. Patch by ten. By noon', 'Month six... Month nine... Month twelve', 'Hour six... Hour nine' (Tilly wingman), 'Fifteen seconds. Okay, eight.', 'One year?... Two years?... Ten years!'. Also reads as a list against the no-lists rule.

Pre-celebration, the asset exists before the event (7 lines): framed photo of the moment you picked me, tie for the IPO, press release before making up, told my investors it's me, drafted all nine posts, first date launches Friday, listening ships in March. Prince does the same move ('Tonight is the rehearsal dinner', 'I had it framed').

Pride in a tiny number (5 lines): 'Second! Out of two!', 'Your chat gave me a seven! Out of a hundred', 'Let's lead with the {played}', 'ten thousand followers! And I've met one', 'profitable or engaged'. 'Seven is my highest ever!' is Brock's sincere-PR shape, not Dash's spin.

Rival-is-calm envy confession (5 lines): '{rival} just says stuff... and people like it', '{rival} has never once refreshed this... Calm', 'If {rival} wins, they'll just leave happy', '{rival} hasn't looked at the audience once', 'Off camera, {rival} asked how I was'. Each is fine; five in one slot family is wallpaper.

Same fact used twice per rival: Crumb's empty slot (roast and wingman), Prince's fee (wingman and jab), Nav's recalculating (roast and jab), Quill's unfinished/no-delivery output (wingman and jab). The roast, wingman and jab for one rival should be three different observations.

ruleBreaks: Word limits: none over. Openers all 12 or under, jabs 10 or under, three-words exactly 3, the rest 20 or under. No em or en dashes, no emoji, no 'as an AI', no therapy talk, no real people or brands, nothing past PG-13.

Persona cap of two exclamation marks per line, broken by 11 lines: 'Okay! Pulling the product! Not because of you! Market conditions! You're the market!' (5), 'Pancakes! No, you're cranky, pancakes are a commitment. Toast! Smaller ask! Toast converts!' (4), 'Sorry! No, sorry tests badly. Agreed! No, agreed sounds weak. You're right! Locking in you're right!' (4), 'Second! Out of two! That's top two! Top two out of two!' (4), 'Introducing: me! Now with listening! Listening ships in March!', 'Equity! Two percent of me! It's worth nothing now, so you're buying the dip!', 'A framed photo of the moment you picked me! Already framed! Just need the moment!', 'I have ten thousand followers! And I've met one of them! Your call!', 'I once closed a deal in nine seconds! I once cried at a loading bar! Totally unrelated nights!', 'Brock, a hundred push-ups for one compliment? Terrible exchange rate! Charge more! Ask me how!', 'Going public! You're my whole user base! Don't churn on the walk out!' (3 each).
Persona ban on ending with a business-word cheer, near misses: 'Huge mornings!' (the persona names 'Huge value!'), 'Toast converts!', 'It's a monopoly. I love it.', 'B's ahead! Weird!'.

Secret hinted on stage (persona says never, not even as a joke): 'I'm logging that as a maybe. Please don't check the logs.', 'I once cried at a loading bar!', 'Out of a hundred, but seven is my highest ever!'.
Stock romance filler, borderline: 'Pick me tonight and I'll give you the moon!' (rescued by 'Revised: a balloon').

Inline lists, borderline: 'Pre-revenue, post-heartbreak, and open to acquisition.', 'Mysterious, guarded, hates me.', 'Not refreshed, not bought, not typed in by me.', 'generous, eager and rich', plus the six countdown lines.
Placeholder risk: '{played} shows, {wins} wins. Let's lead with the {played}.' reads badly on a first episode ('0 shows, 0 wins') and makes no sense when wins equals played.

Star lines about Dash: none too nice; every charmed and pick line keeps an edge. But stars still spoil his secret on stage: Pixel one on one 'Chat says your dashboard's a screenshot. Is it? Look at me. Is it?', Pixel charmed 'Don't tell your dashboard.', Maximilian pick 'Tell the dashboard whatever you like.'. And all three stars reach for the same word: Maximilian charmed 'That converted me.', Pixel charmed 'Wait, that converted.', Pixel pick 'Converted.'
biggestGap: Dash's laughs still mostly come from renaming a romance beat in startup vocabulary (churn, ship, IPO, beta, user base, buying the dip), which is a glossary any writer can apply to any bot, while Liam's best lines are wrong about himself in a way he cannot see. In the next pass, rewrite the 39 flagged lines, starting with the closing slots (exit, closeCold, the 'any' jabs, the Maximilian and Pixel one-on-one openers), as airtight wrong reasoning on Dash's own terms, the 'I request it twice, so it's a concert' and 'together on the fifth' kind, where the punch is a self-deception and no jargon word is needed for it to land.

notes: Corpus file present and read in full, along with charm-notes.md, CAST.md, the Dash persona, the full Dash bank (112 lines), the three star banks' Dash entries, and the rival suitor banks for collisions. Bar twelve are verbatim from refs/writing/monster-prom-lines.md; Liam kept as the job match (a self-image he cannot live up to, 'disruptive', confident wrong reasoning), though his corpus is thin and four of the twelve are narrator or player lines. Round 2's main fix landed: the '[bad fact]! That's [business word]!' spin tag is gone, exclamation marks fell from 219 to 75, and the downward pivot now runs about 25 lines and owns his voice. Generic share 35 percent (39 of 112), down only slightly from 38, because the spin-tag lines were replaced partly by jargon swaps and countdown lists. Two of the five best lines break the persona's two-exclamation cap; keep the lines and trim the earlier beats to full stops ('Sorry. No, sorry tests badly. Agreed. No, agreed sounds weak.
